newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens firmer on German mark weakness.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens firmer on German mark weakness.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3677 (US$0.7311) in light trading on Monday after it jumped against the German mark in overnight trading, dealers said. * They said the mark fell to new lows against major currencies on worries that a broad-based European monetary union will produce a weak euro and cause greater uncertainty in the German currency.
"The buying of the U.S. dollar against the mark brought buyers of Canada in," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.
The continued weakness of the mark followed comments last Thursday by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer who said the U.S. dollar's correction against the mark was over.

Analysts said markets are nervous as the U.S. dollar moves to the key 1.8 marks level from its current 1.7960 marks. "The market knows the Bundesbank is not yet that concerned about dollar/mark to start changing monetary policy," said Klaus Baader, currency economist at Lehman Brothers.
Traders said the Canadian dollar was in an ideal position to benefit from the mark's weakness, especially after the release of strong employment numbers on Monday.
Statistics Canada reported unemployment fell to 9.1 percent in June from 9.5 percent in May, its lowest rate since September 1995.
Employment grew by 51,500 in June compared with growth of 61,000 in the previous month.
"You can expect more firmness today for the Canada (dollar). There's fairly decent demand for it after last Friday's numbers," Farrill said.
The Canadian dollar rose to 83.21 Japanese yen on Monday from 83.16 at Friday's close.
